course_details.Overview of class: This course approaches composition through the fundamental elements of music. We will examine what these elements are, how they have been used, and how far their possibilities have been extended in contemporary musical practices. Through listening, analysis, discussion, and hands-on creative exercises, we will explore how musical materials can be selected, developed, and organized into a composition. The primary focus of the course is the creation of original work. Student composition projects may take many forms, from conventionally notated music to text or graphic scores, electronic sound, improvisation, and experimental performance. No prior composition experience is required.

course_details.Overview of class:
we begin with the question: what could happen if we were to consider material things and instruments as lively agents? Topics include Instrumental Hybrids and "Chimeras", Cybernetics, and Instrumental Augmentations both in the acoustic and digital realms.
Readings including those of Donna Haraway, Karen Barad, and Kevin Toksöz Fairbairn.
Students will become familiar with the artistic practices of performers such as Laetitia Sonami and Chiara Percivati. They will also analyze the repertoire of Nicolas Collins, Malin Bang, Alvin Lucier, and others. A contemporary repertoire focused course.

course_details.Overview of class: The class will survey and discuss aesthetic positions of the 20th and 21st centuries and examine their impact on contemporary music and sound art. A selection of texts that have influenced cultural production and reception will be read, by writers such as Borges, Higgins, Said, Morton, Foucault, Baudrillard, Jameson, Deleuze & Guattari, DeLanda, and others. A central part of the course discussion will be to interrogate the ways that these ideas support, oppose, and elaborate upon each other, and in particular, to observe how the perspectives presented by these writers have served as fodder for contemporary sonic praxes, and ultimately to construct the recently minted traditions that undergird our own sound-making as we enter the second quarter of the 21st Century. We will also be exploring non-linear connections and the conceptual framework of the grid and its utility in assisting those non-linear connections.
course_details.Registration Requirements: Permission numbers are not needed. Freshmen up to doctoral students are welcome. Students must be capable of reading essays and other texts, discussing the content of those texts, and writing short responses (7-10 sentences, on average) to those texts, and to the responses of other students in the class.
course_details.Learning Objectives: Students will have encountered a range of critical texts by important authors.
course_details.Teaching Method: Students read assigned essays and other texts, discuss the content of those texts in class, and wrie short responses (7-10 sentences, on average) to those texts, and to the responses of other students in the class.
course_details.Evaluation Method: Class participation is a crucial part of the course activities, and taken together with the written responses will comprise each student's cumulative grade.
course_details.Class Materials (Required): All reading materials will be distributed via Canvas.
